profile.summary: Mistral-DNA is a family of DNA language models built by shrinking the Mixtral-8x7B mixture-of-experts architecture so it fits on a single GPU. The published checkpoints were pretrained on genome sequences, several on the human hg38 assembly and others on yeast, bacteria, viruses, plants and farm animals. A checkpoint takes a DNA sequence and returns per-token hidden states, which are pooled into an embedding or fine-tuned for a classification task.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: Overview; model card: Model Card, Calculate the embedding; Hugging Face listing

summary_quotes.text: Here the Mixtral model ([Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1)) was modified to significantly reduce the number of parameters mostly by removing layers, such that it could be trained on a GPU such as an RTX3090.
The model was pretrained using 10kb DNA sequences from the hg38 human genome assembly.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each checkpoint is a Mixtral-style model: the card lists grouped-query attention, sliding-window attention, a byte-fallback BPE tokenizer and mixture of experts. The 138M human checkpoint's config gives 8 layers, hidden size 768, 8 attention heads, 8 key-value heads, 8 local experts with 1 expert used per token, a vocabulary of 4096 and max_position_embeddings 512, with sliding_window set to null. Its architecture entry is MixtralForCausalLM. In use, the card takes the hidden states returned by the model and max-pools them into one vector per sequence.
sections.source_locator: config.json; model card: Model Architecture, Calculate the embedding of a DNA sequence

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Fifteen checkpoints are listed on Hugging Face under RaphaelMourad with Mistral-DNA in the name. Four are human (hg38), named 1M, 17M, 138M and 422M; the others cover yeast, bacteria, bacteriophage, plasmid, virus, lncRNA, noncoding sequence, Arabidopsis thaliana, pig, cow and goat. The repository README still points to an older checkpoint named Mistral-DNA-v0.1, which is not in the listing read. A result should name the exact checkpoint and its revision; this page read the 138M human checkpoint at revision 4c3c8c7b.

run_guide.summary: Load the 138M human checkpoint from Hugging Face and compute a max-pooled embedding for one DNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python with pip, PyTorch and transformers. The model card says to use transformers 4.34.0 or newer.
The card's example does not require a GPU. The README's own training setup used an NVIDIA driver 535.129.03 with CUDA 12.2, and says the model was shrunk to train on a GPU such as an RTX3090.
Weights are Apache-2.0 and not gated. The code repository states no licence.

steps.title: Install transformers and PyTorch
steps.explanation: One pip line built from the card's version requirement and the README's torch dependency; neither source gives this exact command.

quotes.text: Ensure you are utilizing a stable version of Transformers, 4.34.0 or newer.

steps.title: Load the model and embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("RaphaelMourad/Mistral-DNA-v1-138M-hg38", trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("RaphaelMourad/Mistral-DNA-v1-138M-hg38", trust_remote_code=True)

DNAseq = "TGATGATTGGCGCGGCTAGGATCGGCT"
inputs = tokenizer(DNAseq, return_tensors = 'pt')["input_ids"]
hidden_states = model(inputs)[0]

embedding_max = torch.max(hidden_states[0], dim=0)[0]
print(embedding_max.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's two code blocks joined and wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the tokenizer and weights, runs one forward pass and prints the pooled embedding's shape.
steps.source_locator: model card: Load the model from huggingface; Calculate the embedding of a DNA sequence

outputs: The shape of the max-pooled embedding vector, printed to the terminal. The card's comment expects 256; the config's hidden size is 768.
limitations: These commands were read from the model card and have not been executed by Rewire.
Loading uses trust_remote_code, so custom model code from the repository is executed.
Pretraining and fine-tuning are offered only as Jupyter notebooks and Google Colab links, not as command-line scripts.
The data generation step needs R and Bioconductor packages.

notes: The GitHub repository has no licence file, so licence is left off the README source and store_bytes is false for it; the Hugging Face cards are Apache-2.0. The README points at a checkpoint named Mistral-DNA-v0.1, which returned an error from the Hugging Face API, so the current v1 family was described instead; a human should decide which checkpoint the GUANinE benchmark evaluated. No paper by the model's own authors was found. The model card's embedding size comment (256) conflicts with the config hidden size (768). The GUANinE paper (PMC13501288, the existing source on this record) says it evaluated two Mistral-DNA models and names Mistral-DNA-422m-hg38 in its table; that text was read but not saved, so it is not quoted here.
